Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 1 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Tropical Depression ISANG
Issued at: 10:30 AM, 22 August 2025(Friday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Bataan, Metro Manila, Cavite, Nueva Ecija, Zambales(Botolan, Cabangan, San Felipe, San Narciso, San Antonio, Subic, Castillejos, San Marcelino, Olongapo) and Batangas(Balayan, Calaca, Calatagan, Laurel, Lian, Nasugbu, Tuy).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Possible FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Laguna, Tarlac, Batangas(Agoncillo, Alitagtag, Balete, Batangas City, Bauan, Tanauan, Cuenca, Ibaan, Lemery, Lipa, Lobo, Mabini, Malvar, Mataasnakahoy, Padre Garcia, Rosario, San Jose, San Juan, San Luis, San Nicolas, San Pascual, Santa Teresita, Santo Tomas, Taal, Talisay, Taysan, Tingloy), Quezon(General Nakar, Infanta, Real, Panukulan, Burdeos, Polillo, Patnanungan, Jomalig) and Zambales(Candelaria, Iba, Masinloc, Palauig, Santa Cruz) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 2:00 PM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.

#MSNews | Heavy rains and flooding caused the cancellation of classes in at least six cities in Metro Manila on Friday, August 22. 

As of 9:30 a.m., suspension of classes in both private and public schools at all levels was announced in the cities of Manila, Paranaque, Las Pinas, Mandaluyong, Pasay, and Muntinlupa because of the bad weather conditions.

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority reported gutter-deep floods on the northbound lane of Roxas Boulevard, Quirino Avenue, United Nations Avenue, and Kalaw, Leveriza Street, Taft Avenue, and Pedro Gil Street, and areas of Philippine Christian University and Philippine General Hospital, all in Manila.

Gutter-deep floods were also reported along Sucat Avenue corner Canaynay Avenue and the northbound lane near Paranaque National High School in Paranaque City; the northbound lane of EDSA Shaw Tunnel in Mandaluyong City; EDSA, Roxas Boulevard, Tramo Street, and Andrews Avenue in Pasay City; and the northbound lane of Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City.

The Mandaluyong City government reported flooded areas along Boni Avenue, Cruz Street, Lopez Street, and Ballesteros Street, all in Barangay Zaniga, and Nueve de Pebrero in Barangay Mauway.

There were also reports of stranded commuters in some parts of Metro Manila. | via Joel Zurbano

For more news updates, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.
